To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the evolution of sustainable design has been influenced by the following key factors: 1) The emergence of new technologies and materials, 2) The development of environmental regulations and standards, 3) The increasing availability of environmental impact data, 4) The emergence of sustainable design tools and methodologies.

the evolution of sustainable design methodologies has been driven by the development and implementation of new tools, which are in turn driven by the need for improved communication and the desire for greater integration of the design process.

the evolution of ecodesign methodologies has been incremental and has not produced the desired ’Factor X’ changes in design, and that the key to future success is a greater understanding of the human factors of design and the development of tools to facilitate this.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we can develop the next generation of ecodesign methods that can deliver radical improvements in the design of products and systems.
the identification of the factors which have contributed to the current state of sustainable design and the development of a research strategy to overcome these limitations.
the development of sustainable product design and its integration into the design process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sustainable design is still in the early stages of its development, and there is still a long way to go to achieve the full potential benefits of sustainability.
sustainable design is still a developing area, and the future is bright.
the current practice of sustainable design methodologies is in a state of transition, which is driven by a number of key influencing factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to move from a linear to a circular economy, and that this is a challenge that requires the full involvement of the whole value chain.
we are in a position to move towards the next generation of sustainable design tools, which will enable designers to make radical improvements to the sustainability of their products and services.
we have shown that ecodesign and sustainable design are not static concepts, and that they are constantly evolving in response to changes in the wider context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current state of sustainable design methodologies and tools are not sufficient to enable the next generation of radical sustainable product designs.
a holistic approach is needed in order to address sustainability challenges, and that this can be achieved through the integration of existing tools, techniques and methods, as well as new ones.
the next generation of design methodologies will need to be able to support the designer in making radical changes to the product design process, rather than just incremental improvements.
